The '''1995–96 Serie A''' title was won by [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] (15th title for the Milan-based club), with [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] finishing as runners-up. Fourth placed [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] tasted glory in the [[Coppa Italia]], while seventh-placed [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] only narrowly managed to qualify for the [[UEFA Cup]] under the management of their new [[England|English]] head coach [[Roy Hodgson]]. In fact Internazionale needed both Fiorentina beating Atalanta in the 1995–96 Coppa Italia Final and their (Internazionale's) arch-rivals AC Milan and Juventus win the Serie A (Milan) and the 1995–96 UEFA Champions League Final (Juventus). Had one of these three things not occurred Internazionale would have missed out on european football for the second time in four years (having failed to qualify for any of the 1992–93 UEFA club competitions). [[F.C. Bari 1908|Bari]], [[Torino F.C.|Torino]], [[U.S. Cremonese|Cremonese]] and [[Calcio Padova|Padova]] were all relegated.

==Teams==
[[Piacenza Calcio|Piacenza]], [[Udinese]], [[Vicenza Calcio|Vicenza]] and [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] had been promoted from [[Serie B]].
